Article Title: 'Padma Bhushan small thing, make him PM': Cong mocks BJP Bengal chief's praise for CEC

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Pawan Khera on Saturday hit back at West Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya after the latter said Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar deserved the Padma Bhushan for his role in conducting the state’s recent assembly election and revising the voter list.Reacting to Bhattacharya’s remarks, Khera said, "The Padma Bhushan is a very small thing. Make him the Prime Minister. After all, a person who can make others Prime Minister should be made one himself."Bhattacharya had earlier praised the CEC while speaking to reporters at Panihati in North 24 Parganas district, saying the CEC deserved the Padma Bhushan "at the very least". He credited Kumar with ensuring a violence-free election in West Bengal and with "cleansing" the electoral roll by removing illegal Bangladeshi immigrants."Gyanesh Kumar deserves to be awarded, at the very least, with the Padma Bhushan. The people of West Bengal are delighted that, after so long, intimidation was kept at bay, that there were no incidents of murder during the elections and people were actually allowed to cast their votes," the BJP leader said.He also claimed that Kumar had played a key role in the revision of the voter list."In a border state like West Bengal, Gyanesh Kumar took the initiative to remove the names of Bangladeshi infiltrators from the voter list," Bhattacharya said."The people of West Bengal have rarely witnessed an election like this. Therefore, the general public of West Bengal is grateful to Gyanesh Kumar and has blessed him with all their hearts," he added.The BJP leader’s comments came amid a growing controversy over the functioning of the Election Commission during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. An Indian Express report said that two election commissioners had objected to decisions allegedly taken in their names have triggered criticism from the Opposition.Also read: Unease within NDA over EC-SIR row? Three BJP allies seek poll body clarification as opposition keeps up pressure Congress has held nationwide protests demanding Kumar’s removal and arrest, while a plea has also been filed in the Supreme Court challenging election-related orders and alleged software changes attributed to the CEC without the concurrence of the other two election commissioners.The row has also drawn criticism from Rahul Gandhi , who accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and Kumar of being "traitors" and alleged that they were destroying the foundation of India’s democracy by rigging elections.Bhattacharya, however, dismissed Gandhi’s remarks, saying, "The Congress itself doesn't pay heed to him. His own party doesn't take him seriously, and you are talking of Rahul Gandhi."
Article Summary: West bengal bjp chief samik bhattacharya said chief election commissioner gyanesh kumar deserved the padma bhushan. He credited kumar with ensuring a violence-free election in west bengal and with "cleansing" the electoral roll. Congress has held nationwide protests demanding kumar’s removal and arrest.

Article Title: NDA ally Jitan Ram Manjhi seeks more speaking time for SC/ST MPs in Parliament
Article Text:
Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi asked the Speaker to issue necessary directions to the concerned authorities.

NDA differences over SC/ST reservation

NEW DELHI: Union minister and NDA ally Jitan Ram Manjhi has written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, backing a BJP MP’s request for adequate speaking time for MPs from the Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) communities during parliamentary discussions on important bills.In his letter, Manjhi said BJP MP Gajendra Singh Patel, who represents Khargone in Madhya Pradesh, had raised the issue during an “NDA MPs Group Dialogue Meeting” held at Manjhi’s Delhi residence on August 5.Patel had specifically requested that SC/ST MPs be given sufficient opportunity to raise issues concerning their communities on the floor of the House, Manjhi said.The Union minister has asked the Speaker to take further action on Patel’s request and issue necessary directions to the concerned authorities.Speaking to PTI, Patel confirmed that he had raised the issue and said the time allocated to SC/ST MPs should be increased further, as the speaking time allotted to each political party is divided among its MPs.“It is not that we do not get time, but we should get more time. More issues concerning SC/ST communities should be raised,” he said.Patel said the request was aimed at ensuring that issues concerning SC/ST communities receive adequate space during parliamentary discussions, while acknowledging that MPs from these communities do get opportunities to speak.Earlier last month, differences within the NDA came to the fore over the contentious issue of sub-categorisation of SC/ST reservations, with Manjhi and fellow Bihar-based Union minister Chirag Paswan taking divergent positions on the question of reviewing the reservation system.The debate intensified after HAM(S) president and Bihar minister Santosh Kumar Suman reiterated his party’s demand for sub-categorisation of SC/ST reservations, arguing that the most deprived communities should receive a greater share of the benefits.The Supreme Court’s August 1, 2024 Constitution Bench judgment allowing states to create sub-categories within SC and ST reservations has added a new dimension to the debate.Chirag strongly opposed any review of reservation and said Manjhi and his son should resign if they supported such measures.“The constitutional provision of SC/ST reservation is based on social discrimination and not economic status. If they want to change the Constitution, then debate the issue in Parliament. Those who talk or think about reviewing reservation should first resign, as they actually want to completely end it and reduce its scope,” Chirag said.He maintained that reservation was in place yesterday, is in place today and would continue in the future.Reacting to Chirag’s demand, Suman said he was ready to resign. “As far as resignations go, we are ready. My younger brother’s party is the bigger one; they have more numbers than us and are politically third-generation too — so let them take the lead. Let him step forward by resigning and we are prepared to resign alongside him,” he said.Suman maintained that reviewing reservation did not mean abolishing it. He said HAM(S) was seeking sub-categorisation, or a “quota within a quota”, so that communities at the bottom of the social and economic hierarchy could benefit.He cited Musahar, Bhuiyan, Dom, Halkhor and Nat communities as groups that continue to face deprivation and discrimination.JD(U) national general secretary and MLA Shyam Rajak, meanwhile, opposed any discussion on reviewing reservation and warned that tampering with the system could create serious social tensions. He said reservation was a constitutional right, not charity.The reservation debate has particular political significance in Bihar, where Dalit communities are socially diverse. The Nitish Kumar government introduced the Mahadalit category in 2007 to identify the most deprived Dalit communities.
Article Summary: Union minister jitan ram manjhi has written to lok sabha speaker om birla. He has backed a bjp mp’s request for adequate speaking time for mps from the scheduled caste (sc) and scheduled tribe (st) communities.

NEW DELHI: Karnataka home minister Congress leader Priyank Kharge on Saturday took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi after he shared a video of himself attending a “Bhajan Clubbing” event in Delhi, questioning his response to issues concerning the Election Commission.“PM @narendramodi has time for ‘Bhajan Clubbing’, but no time to answer serious questions about the clubbing of democracy through the Election Commission. Article Title: 'Dubai-based scammers looted Rs 94,000 crore': CBI arrests Mahadev app key accused deported from UAE
Article Text:

CBI on Thursday arrested Abhishek Kumar, a key accused in the Mahadev online betting and gambling case in which Enforcement Directorate (ED) has claimed that the perpetrators of the illegal activities have so far generated and laundered proceeds of crime of more than Rs 94,000 crore.Kumar was deported from the UAE and taken into custody by CBI immediately after he arrived at Hyderabad airport from Dubai. He was close to main accused Saurabh Chandrakar and Shubham Soni - both continue to operate the gambling network from the UAE and other jurisdictions.Kumar coordinated various panels in the Mahadev network and was responsible for collecting funds and acquiring immovable assets in Dubai out of ill-gotten proceeds of crime, a CBI spokesperson said. He has been taken to Raipur and produced before a special court for police remand. So far, seven Red Corner Notices and two extradition requests have been pending against other accused.The Mahadev online betting and gambling app is still active and proceeds of crime of Rs 94,000 crore have been generated so far by the accused, who are in Dubai, ED has said in its latest chargesheet in the case. More than Rs 1,000 crore has been invested in Indian share markets through foreign portfolio investments (FPIs), the agency said.It estimated that in the last few years, the accused generated more than Rs 11,000 crore annually from illegal online gambling and betting activities.Based on analysis of various seized digital evidence and statements of several accused, ED said that "it can be estimated that proceeds of crime worth Rs 11,400 crore (approx) must have been generated by illegal operations of Mahadev online book every year". The gambling network has been running since 2019."As per latest findings, Mahadev app is still running a huge number of panels. Estimated proceeds of crime generated by the app is around Rs 75,000-80,000 crore during the last seven years," ED has said. In addition, it said other illegal apps run by the syndicate like Skyexchange.com and Lotus365.com have generated proceeds of crime of over Rs 14,000 crore."A majority of the proceeds of crime was layered and transferred to the promoters based in Dubai," ED stated.The agency has so far attached assets worth over Rs 2,000 crore linked to various accused. The agency said the above estimation of proceeds of crime is only a provisional figure and is likely to go up.
Article Summary: Abhishek kumar was deported from the uae and taken into custody by cbi. : Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said Thursday he feared he could be subjected to an “encounter” for speaking out against what he called atrocities in Ladakh, a year after police firing killed four protesters in Leh.Drawing a comparison with Tibet, Wangchuk said Ladakhis had chosen India because of its democracy. “Today, such atrocities are being committed in Ladakh that even China is not doing in Tibet. That is what you are seeing today,” he said, addressing a gathering on the first anniversary of the police firing on Sept 24, 2025.He sought a people’s tribunal to probe the killings, saying a judicial commission set up by Union home ministry had yet to submit its report.“Last year on this day, four people died... After 170 days, Union govt withdrew his detention on March 14 this year and he was set free.He feared further action, saying: “They sent me to jail. Inquiries have been made against me. Wangchuk accused authorities of stopping people from attending the rally, a claim denied by police.Police said Ladakh Buddhist Association had sought permission for a public meeting at Leh’s NDS stadium, which has a capacity of 10,000. Police reported a turnout of 800 at the event and denied allegations that they erected barricades to stop people from reaching the venue.

Article Title: Centre pleads for prospective effect of SC creamy layer ruling
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Facing the task of implementing Supreme Court's ruling on calculating creamy layer criteria for OBC reservation from the retrospective date of 2012, Centre pleaded with the court to make the enforcement of the verdict prospective and grant it two years' time to implement it.The court had in March held that the income of parents could not be the sole criterion to determine the creamy layer of a candidate for exclusion from OBC reservation, and status and category of a parent's job had to be considered with an 'income/wealth test' as an additional criterion. It made the verdict implementable from 2012, when the case was first filed.In a written note filed by additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, govt submitted that the retrospective application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the time and create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression."The retrospective implementation of the present judgement would create changes in candidates' service and cadre allocation... as it would affect the services of persons appointed on the basis of CSE-2012 onward and cause a cascading effect among civil servants... The aforementioned cascading effect will impact not only OBC candidates but also reverberate across all categories including (unreserved category) of the civil services," the note said.Govt said a reasonable time of two years should be given to it to undertake the necessary exercise of establishing equivalence of posts, after consulting all the stakeholders and formulating a uniform policy/mechanism for determination of OBC creamy layer status."Union of India is only praying for a limited deferral of the operationalisation of the law laid down by this hon'ble court for a period of two years so that the competing rights can be adjusted consistent with the administrative contingencies and an effective equivalence exercise is carried out," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme court's ruling on calculating creamy layer criteria for obc reservation from retrospective date of 2012. Centre pleaded with the court to make the enforcement of the verdict prospective and grant it two years' time to implement it.

Article Title: NALSAR students screen Umar Khalid documentary after screenings cancelled at IIIT-Hyderabad, NLSIU
Article Text:
The screening was a private event restricted to students.

Prisoner No. 626710 is Present

Hyderabad: The screening of Umar Khalid’s documentary,, which was cancelled at the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad (IIIT-H), and National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, was held at NALSAR University of Law in the city on Wednesday evening. A group of students who independently organised the “solidarity screening” said it was held to offer an opportunity “to engage directly with the film’s questions about rights, accountability and the human cost of prolonged incarceration, while expressing solidarity with those affected by these failures of the justice system”.The screening was a private event restricted to students.“The film raises urgent concerns about the delay in the justice system, and about undertrial prisoners being kept in custody for years without their trials even beginning,” one of the students told TOI via email. “When a person remains imprisoned for six years without trial, the delay itself becomes a serious denial of justice. Law cannot, and should not, be used as a tool of violence without convictions. The process cannot become the punishment,” the email added.NALSAR students have called on student bodies across universities to organise similar screenings of the documentary.The documentary has not been certified by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC).The board has stated that screening an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been obtained.Last week, the screening at IIIT-H was cancelled after the CBFC flagged the issue on X. The institute later said that the proposed event had not been organised or authorised by its management. At NLSIU, too, the event, which was initially postponed, was later cancelled after organisers said they faced threats of criminal action, intimidation, doxxing and other forms of harassment., directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, is a documentary about Khalid, tracing his journey from student activist to his arrest in 2020 and subsequent incarceration.Meanwhile, NALSAR vice-chancellor, Prof Srikrishna Deva Rao, said, “NALSAR University of Law did not authorise screening of the documentary film Prisoner No 626710 on its campus. No official permission for the same was given to anybody by any University authority,”
Article Summary: The screening was a private event restricted to students. Nalsar students have called on student bodies across universities to organise similar screenings of the documentary. The documentary has not been certified by the central board of film certification (cbfc) the board has stated that screening an uncertified film would violate the cinematograph act unless a specific exemption has been obtained.

NEW DELHI: Is Uttar Pradesh all set to go the Bihar way for the opposition’s INDIA bloc? Wait, we are not talking about the results yet. This is about the all-too-familiar alliance strains between INDIA bloc allies - the Samajwadi Party and the Congress in the run-up to UP assembly elections early next year.On Thursday, Akhilesh Yadav unveiled the Samajwadi Party's 'PDA Rath' which he will use for a statewide campaign in the run-up to the 2027 assembly poll. While his fight is against the BJP, the first stop of his rath was Raebareli - a Congress bastion represented by the Gandhis for decades.Also, while Akhilesh targeted the BJP, he had a clear message for the Congress also.“Alliance will happen. We will also go with the alliance. Winnability will be the criteria for deciding seats. For us, it is not about seats, it is about victory. Whosoever can win can take the seat.”The BJP was quick to take digs at both allies and suggested that now Congress should start its campaign from Yadav bastion Mainpuri.This was not an isolated remark. The SP and the Congress have been engaged in a war of words over seat sharing for quite some time now. The open fight has an uncanny resemblance to how events had unfolded between the INDIA bloc allies in Bihar.Cut to the 2025 Bihar assembly elections.INDIA bloc allies - the RJD and the Congress engaged in a continuous war of words in Bihar over seat-sharing and CM face, while the BJP-led NDA managed a smooth division of seats. What started as public posturing between INDIA bloc allies ended up in public sparring between them as the divided opposition alliance was decimated in the polls.The two parties campaigned separately for most of the time as they could not agree on seat sharing. They took out separate yatras across the state. While Rahul Gandhi undertook the “Vote Adhikar Yatra,” RJD’s Tejashwi Yadav went across the state with his “Bihar Adhikar Yatra.” Ironically, it was the success of the two yatras that boomeranged on the alliance as it made seat-sharing bitter and difficult.In the run-up to the Bihar elections, Tejashwi Yadav was confident of a sweep. The Congress was also not willing to budge, guided by its improved showing in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in the state. The two parties used pressure tactics against each other. So much so that the INDIA bloc went into the elections as a divided house despite last-minute agreements and adjustments to keep the alliance intact.Uttar Pradesh appears to be headed the same way, at least as of now. We have already seen a lot of public posturing and sparring between the leaders of the INDIA bloc partners. Both the Congress and the SP have repeatedly claimed that the opposition’s fight against the BJP can be led only by their respective leaders.The SP and Congress contested the 2024 Lok Sabha polls together in Uttar Pradesh and won 43 seats between them, with the SP winning 37 and the Congress six. The alliance also won the Faizabad seat, which includes Ayodhya, where the BJP won in 2019.And that is perhaps where lies the genesis of this power tussle. Both the SP and the Congress feel that it was their party and leader who played a greater role in the 2024 electoral success and hence want the advantage to flow accordingly in seat sharing for the assembly elections.One look at the latest broadside between the two parties and we know why seat sharing between them may not be smooth.Recently, Samajwadi Party MP from Kairana Iqra Hasan and Congress MP from Saharanpur Imran Masood, both elected in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls as part of the SP-Congress alliance, publicly pitched their respective party leaders to take on the BJP."Only Rahul Gandhi is the opposition voice across the country, which unnerves the BJP. Rahul ji has done the hard work and created a favourable atmosphere. So make no mistake, nothing is possible without Rahul ji, and no one should have any doubts about this," Masood said.Days later, Hasan responded and pitched SP chief Yadav as the key to the alliance's prospects."Only Akhilesh Yadav is capable of defeating the BJP. On its own, the Congress won't be able to achieve much," she said.Last week, Congress Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam signalled a firm stance regarding upcoming electoral negotiations and said that any seat-sharing arrangement with the Samajwadi Party (SP) must be built on mutual respect and equal standing.Clarifying reports regarding seat distribution, Gautam claimed that formal discussions with the SP have not yet begun. While expressing open flexibility for minor adjustments, he stressed that the Congress would not compromise its organisational self-respect or dignity in any prospective deal."We have made one thing very clear. The Congress is the country's oldest party. It was the Congress that led the freedom struggle. Any alliance formed will be based on mutual respect; there will be equal partnership and dignity. Sure, we can show some flexibility; there might be minor adjustments, but we cannot compromise on our dignity," the Congress leader said.The contrasting assertions come despite messages of unity from both sides of the divide. Akhilesh is riding high on SP’s Lok Sabha success in Uttar Pradesh. The Congress, which is trying hard to revive its lost electoral fortunes, does not want to compromise on its expansion plans in one of the most politically important states.The problem is that both the parties are wooing the same social base in the state - minorities, Dalits, women, youth. Akhilesh is missing no opportunity to expand his PDA’s - Pichda Dalit and Alpsankhyak - base by making concerted attempts to include Pandits, Aadhi aabadi (women) and other social groups. The Congress is also wooing the Brahmins, the Dalits and the women in a big way.What the two bickering allies don't realise that there are several other parties who are also reaching out to the same social base. For instance, Mayawati and Chandrashekhar Azad are also going all out to woo Dalits. Then there is Owaisi, who has already put both the parties in a Catch22 situation by offering them an alliance against the BJP. Owaisi's proposal is like a double-edged sword for the two parties. If they accept his offer, the BJP will gun for them.If they reject the offer, Owaisi will use the rejection to rally the Muslims against them.The Samjawadi Party and the Congress may do well to learn lessons from the Bihar debacle before it’s too late. Lok Sabha elections and assembly elections are two very different games and success in one does not automatically translate into success in another. There are numerous instances to show that alliances which did well in Lok Sabha elections failed in assembly elections. Maharashtra is a case in point. The Maha Vikas Aghadi of the opposition parties - Congress, Shiv Sena and the NCP did very well in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, putting the BJP on the backfoot. But a year later in 2025 - the opposition alliance was decimated by the BJP in the assembly elections. So, Akhilesh and Rahul need to decide if they want to keep on flexing muscles at each other or unite in time to pose a challenge to the BJP.
Article Summary: Akhilesh yadav unveiled samajwadi party's 'pda rath' which he will use for a statewide campaign in the run-up to the 2027 assembly poll. The open fight has an uncanny resemblance to how events had unfolded between the india bloc allies in bihar.

NEW DELHI: Air India has suspended a pilot who was reportedly found tipsy when he was to operate a Zurich-Delhi flight earlier this month. The Zurich-Delhi flight of Sept 6 had to be rescheduled after the pilot was found unfit to operate the same and till alternate crew was arranged. Any confirmed breach of established protocols is dealt with firmly, with disciplinary action taken in accordance with applicable regulations and company policies. This approach is consistent with Air India's longstanding policy that safety-related violations, particularly those involving alcohol, prohibited substances or conduct that could compromise operational safety, are treated with the utmost seriousness," the official added.Following the recent instances of crew failing dope and breath analyser (for alcohol) tests, AI says it has "has reinforced its expectations of professional conduct and regulatory compliance through multiple interventions across the organisation. A communication from the head of flight operations was issued to all pilots reiterating the airline's zero-tolerance policy towards the use of prohibited substances and reporting for duty under the influence of alcohol or drugs."The communication underscored the responsibilities associated with operating an aircraft and reaffirmed that there can be no compromise on safety, integrity or regulatory compliance.... Air India conducts regular awareness and compliance programmes for pilots and other employees (focussing on) regulatory obligations and licensing requirements; professional conduct standards; substance abuse regulations. ...."

Article Title: In a first, waste plastic mixed with bitumen in pilot test section of NH-44
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a first for the road sector, govt has used waste plastic as a wet mix with bitumen to lay a bituminous highway stretch, a move that is likely to reduce imports of the key construction material while addressing the growing problem of plastic waste.On Thursday, a pilot test section was laid on the main carriageway of NH-44 in Jhansi. Officials associated with the pilot said the technology has potential to reduce conventional bitumen consumption by around 4%, lowering demand for a material that India largely imports to meet domestic requirements. They added that the modified bitumen could cost around 20% less than conventional bitumen.The waste plastic wet-process technology for producing premium-quality Waste Plastic Modified Bitumen (W-PMB 76-10) has been developed by IIT (BHU), Varanasi, under a research programme funded by the ministry of road transport and highways. The performance of the pilot stretch will be monitored by IIT (BHU) to assess its long-term engineering performance and field suitability, officials said.India generates around 25,000 tonne of plastic waste every day. Until now, waste plastic has been used in road construction only as a dry mix with aggregates while laying the bituminous layer. The new method mixes processed waste plastic directly with bitumen before it is laid, making it the first such pilot on a national highway.Officials said the technology offers multiple benefits, including the value-added reuse of waste plastic through a scientifically controlled process and improved rut resistance of bituminous mixes under high ambient temperatures and heavy axle loads.The technology has also recently been granted a patent. The low-density polyethylene (LDPE) used in the process — a soft, flexible and lightweight thermoplastic made from petroleum — includes discarded irrigation pipes, waste files and plastic folders. The material has been processed with the support of local recyclers and MSMEs, creating an opportunity to integrate local waste recycling with infrastructure development.“Laboratory evaluations have shown that LDPE-modified bitumen provides better resistance to moisture damage and greater resistance to rutting at high temperatures. The modified binder increases the stiffness and high-temperature performance of asphalt, helping pavements withstand permanent deformation under heavy traffic loads and extreme temperatures,” an official said.
Article Summary: India generates around 25,000 tonne of plastic waste every day. A pilot test section was laid on the main carriageway of nh-44 in jhansi. Officials associated with the pilot said the technology has potential to reduce conventional bitumen consumption by around 4%.

Article Title: ‘Gyanesh Kumar deserves at least Padma Bhushan’: Bengal BJP chief backs CEC

NEW DELHI: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya has come out strongly in support of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid a growing Congress-led campaign against him. Bhattacharya said that Kumar deserves "at the very least, the Padma Bhushan " for overseeing peaceful elections and changes to the electoral rolls in the state.Bhattacharya also took a swipe at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , claiming that even members of his own party do not take his statements seriously."The fact is, even the Congress party itself doesn't heed Rahul Gandhi's words; they don't take him seriously... Gyanesh Kumar deserves, at the very least, the Padma Bhushan," Bhattacharya said while speaking to reporters.Praising the conduct of elections in West Bengal, the BJP leader said voters were able to cast their ballots without fear or intimidation."The people of West Bengal are delighted that, after so long, intimidation was kept at bay. There were no incidents of murder, and people were actually allowed to cast their votes. Furthermore, in a border state like this, Gyanesh Kumar took the initiative to remove the names of Bangladeshi infiltrators from the voter lists," he added.Bhattacharya said the measures taken by the Election Commission had received broad public support."The people of West Bengal have rarely witnessed an election like this. Therefore, the general public of West Bengal fully supports Gyanesh Kumar..." he said.His remarks came as Congress stepped up its protests against the Election Commission across the country, with party workers demanding Kumar's resignation over the poll body's functioning and the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.In Delhi, the Indian Youth Congress marched from Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar, raising slogans against the CEC and demanding his resignation.The protests also spread across several states. In Chandigarh, similar scenes were reported as police used water cannons against protesting Congress workers, some of whom climbed onto police vans.Congress workers also held demonstrations in Jammu and Kashmir, Assam, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and Manipur.In Shimla, Congress leaders and workers protested outside the State Election Commission office over issues concerning the Election Commission. Article Title: Omar brings J&K statehood resolution to assembly, autonomy mention sparks BJP furore
Article Text:
JK CM Omar Abdullah

SRINAGAR: Chief minister Omar Abdullah brought Friday an assembly resolution seeking restoration of full statehood for J&K, but an autonomy reference ignited a BJP backlash, with its members ripping up copies amid anti-national chants directed at the governing National Conference (NC).The contentious reference came as the document cited an autonomy resolution passed by the assembly in June 2000 when J&K was a state.For nearly two years, Omar has called on the Centre to restore statehood. Soon after taking office, his cabinet passed a resolution to this effect. NC legislators argued that the Centre’s lack of movement forced the party to bring the resolution to the assembly.Omar echoed the sentiment, saying it seems the cabinet was not seen as the sole voice of the people by the Centre, while the legislature represents a broader political spectrum as it includes parties outside govt. “Statehood is not about govt or my family. It is about J&K. That is why we brought it to the House so that a united voice can go to the Centre,” the CM said.As BJP legislators shouted slogans and tore copies, members of NC ally Congress supported the resolution and confronted rivals. CPM, Peoples Conference and PDP also backed the resolution.Leader of opposition, BJP’s Sunil Sharma, accused Omar of trying to “smuggle in” the 2000 autonomy move dressed up as a “statehood restoration resolution”.He recalled that then PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s govt had rejected the 2000 resolution and asserted that BJP will not tolerate its revival now. Angered by this, some NC legislators displayed banners reading “we want autonomy of J&K be restored.” Others called for restoration of Article 370.Omar argued that statehood was a promise made by the Centre and reaffirmed by PM Narendra Modi at an event where Sharma was present. “Delimitation was carried out. Elections were held (in 2024). People voted without any coercion. But the third step of the promise, restoration of statehood, was not fulfilled,” Omar said, citing assurances given by the Centre in Parliament and Supreme Court.Explaining the reference to previous resolutions, the CM said the aim was to convey that the House continued to stand by all past decisions. “Our friends shouldn’t say that we have given up on them. Those resolutions remain in place. This resolution neither replaces nor ignores them. It is an addition to them,” the CM said. The expression “friends” was seen as an allusion to PDP.Speaking to reporters later, Omar rejected BJP’s charges and asked “how demanding statehood can be anti-national”. The CM has been under pressure for several months now, accused by rivals of dropping demands to restore Article 370 and demanding statehood only. Friday’s resolution is not for autonomy, but NC hopes its mention in the document will help it fend off the charges.
Article Summary: Jk cm omar abdullah brought friday an assembly resolution seeking restoration of full statehood for j&k. An autonomy reference ignited a bjp backlash, with its members ripping up copies amid anti-national chants directed at the governing national conference (nc) the contentious reference came as the document cited an autonomy resolution passed by the assembly in june 2000.

Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami , in view of the red alert issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) for the next two days, spoke to Secretary Disaster Management and Rehabilitation Vinod Kumar Suman and directed all concerned districts and departments to take necessary precautionary measures.Dhami directed officials to maintain heightened vigilance in districts under red and orange alerts, continuously monitor vulnerable areas and ensure that all arrangements for relief and rescue operations are in place in advance in case of any emergency. He also directed that district emergency operation centres remain active and weather warnings be disseminated immediately at the local level.Disaster management and rehabilitation minister Madan Kaushik also spoke to Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman and took stock of the weather situation and preparedness across the state. He directed officials to closely monitor the weather and remain fully prepared to deal with any eventuality.Following the chief minister’s directions, Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman held a meeting with all 13 districts on Friday and instructed them to remain on alert mode.According to the weather department forecast, on September 26, red alerts have been issued for five districts, orange alerts for five districts and yellow alerts for three districts.On September 27, red alerts have been issued for four districts, orange alerts for four districts and yellow alerts for five districts.On September 26, Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Nainital and Udham Singh Nagar are under a red alert, while Dehradun, Pauri Garhwal, Rudraprayag, Chamoli and Almora are under an orange alert. Haridwar, Uttarkashi and Tehri Garhwal are under a yellow alert.On September 27, red alerts have been issued for Dehradun, Tehri Garhwal, Pauri Garhwal and Haridwar; orange alerts for Uttarkashi, Chamoli, Nainital and Rudraprayag; and yellow alerts for Bageshwar, Almora, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar and Pithoragarh.The weather department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall at several places and extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places. Authorities have been asked to remain particularly vigilant in view of the possibility of landslides and road blockages in hilly areas, rising water levels in rivers and streams, and waterlogging in the plains.Suman directed all districts to continuously monitor vulnerable areas, keep district emergency operation centres operational and ensure immediate dissemination of every weather warning to the ground level.Officials have been instructed to continuously monitor water levels in rivers, streams, gad-gaderas and other water sources and make arrangements to shift people living nearby to safer locations if water levels rise. JCBs and other necessary machinery should be stationed at strategic locations along landslide-prone roads and areas so that blocked routes can be cleared at the earliest.All district emergency operation centres have been directed to remain operational round the clock, with continuous coordination among the police, SDRF, fire services, health, Public Works Department, drinking water, power and other concerned departments. Relief and rescue teams, along with necessary equipment and resources, should be deployed in vulnerable areas as required.The secretary also directed that traffic on mountain routes be regulated based on weather and road conditions and unnecessary travel in areas vulnerable to landslides and heavy rainfall be avoided. People living near rivers, streams and seasonal water channels should be regularly alerted and prevented from approaching riverbanks or entering fast-flowing waters.Special monitoring has also been ordered along the Char Dham routes, major tourist destinations and other vulnerable areas to ensure the safety of pilgrims and tourists. All arrangements should be kept ready in advance so that relief and rescue operations can begin with minimum response time in case of an emergency.Suman urged district administrations to remain fully alert and not to show any negligence in view of the prevailing weather conditions. He also appealed to the public to follow advisories issued by the weather department and district administration, avoid unnecessary travel and stay away from rivers, streams and landslide-prone areas.The State Emergency Operation Centre is continuously monitoring the weather situation. In case of any emergency, people can contact the State Emergency Operation Centre at toll-free number 1070, the District Emergency Operation Centre at 1077, or emergency services at 112.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister pushkar singh dhami spoke to secretary disaster management and rehabilitation vinod kumar suman. He directed officials to maintain heightened vigilance in districts under red and orange alerts, continuously monitor vulnerable areas and ensure that all arrangements for relief and rescue operations are in place in case of any emergency.

Article Title: When food becomes a philosophy
Article Text:
“Pon karaya kaayum, mann karaya peyyum”

Pathitrupathu

Pulal Maruththal

“Kollaan Pulalai Maruththaanai Kaikooppi

Ella Uyirum Thozhum.”

ahimsa

Chandogya Upanishad

Purataasi arrives with the fragrance of devotion. The sixth month of the Tamil calendar, dedicated to Lord Vishnu, is a month when many Tamil households voluntarily give up non-vegetarian food . Even confirmed meat lovers submit to this discipline. Some of my friends go berserk on the last day of Aavani, indulging in every imaginable meat delicacy!But Purataasi is more than a month of prayer. It is also a month of climatic transition. An old Tamil saying describes its extremes vividly:— the heat is so fierce that gold may melt, and the rain so heavy that the earth may erode. Perhaps, a gentler diet could give the digestive system some respite while the body adjusted to the changing weather.Vegetarianism itself must have emerged much later in the journey of humankind. Our earliest ancestors were certainly hunters and meat-eaters., in Sangam literature for instance, describes a preparation in which red meat was cooked with pulses and mixed with white rice — a dish that sounds remarkably like a distant ancestor of today's biryani.And yet, Thiruvalluvar gave vegetarianism an extraordinary ethical dimension. He devoted an entire chapter to— the refusal of meat. In Kural 260, he says:“One who does not kill and refuses to eat meat is worshipped by all living beings.”Valluvar did not present vegetarianism merely as a religious injunction. He seemed to locate it in something more elemental — compassion. His argument begins not with food, but with the refusal to cause harm.This has naturally led some scholars to see a possible Jain influence in Valluvar's thought. Jainism places, or non-violence, at the heart of spiritual life, and vegetarianism became one of its most rigorous expressions. The Jain understanding of food is deeply connected with the avoidance of harm and the accumulation of karma.The Jain tradition traces a powerful story of renunciation to Prince Neminatha, regarded as the 22nd Tirthankara. Neminatha was on his way to his wedding when he heard the cries of animals gathered to be slaughtered for the wedding feast. He turned away from the marriage, renounced his royal life and embraced the path of a Jain monk. The story transforms food into a moral question: what price should another life pay for our appetite?Interestingly, thespeaks of a teacher who instructed Krishna in asceticism and non-violence. Historian D D Kosambi suggested that this teacher may have been Neminatha himself, though this remains a historical conjecture.Today, vegetarianism has acquired another dimension. The growing popularity of veganism in the West is partly driven by concerns about animal welfare and the environmental footprint of livestock farming. Yet, paradoxically, in India — traditionally home to the world's largest vegetarian population — dietary habits are increasingly moving in the opposite direction.Perhaps the enduring wisdom of Valluvar lies not in telling us what must be on our plate, but in asking what lies within our heart. For him, refusing meat was not simply about food. It was about whether the mind could remain indifferent to the suffering of another living being.Sometimes, what we choose not to consume can reveal more about us than what we eat.
Article Summary: The sixth month of the tamil calendar, dedicated to lord vishnu, is a month when many tamil households voluntarily give up non-vegetarian food. The growing popularity of veganism in the west is partly driven by concerns about animal welfare and the environmental footprint of livestock farming.
